pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: lib/articles/agentSteps.ts:82 Each headless writer session is dispatched under only enforced caps (timeoutMin, and --max-budget-usd added by the loop guard), while the brief built above it carries no derived turn or cost budget and no early-stop conditions, so the soft-budget-under-the-hard-cap pair of limits is missing and a cap-fired turn is just a failed step rather than a measured cap-fired fraction.

techniques.evidence: lib/articles/agentSteps.ts:82 Hard caps only. promptSlots (prompt.ts) has no turn or cost budget slot, and the only round count in the brief (MAX_ROUNDS) equals the cap instead of sitting below it.
lib/articles/store.ts:232 run.json status comes from the closed ARTICLE_STATUSES vocabulary, and updateRun is the one door that refuses an illegal transition, whoever asks for it.
lib/articles/store.ts:235 Every accepted transition is written durably with tmp+rename under a cross-process lock before the call returns.

lib/articles/ingestDraft.ts:36 The parent reads and validates the declared out/ artifacts (ingestResearch, ingestOutline, ingestPost) on top of the outcome check at agentSteps.ts:93. It does not take the agent's word that it finished.

lib/articles/loop.ts:451 Every dispatched topic gets a roster row before any work starts, and each row ends classified as at-the-gate, ceiling-stopped, halted or failed. Orphaned and damaged runs are reported too.
lib/articles/loop.ts:450 A row whose run has not yet been read carries an explicit "unknown" member, not a guessed status.
lib/articles/loop.ts:386 Slot cap at the loop's one dispatch door, plus a run-total budget (loop.ts:511) that defers the next launch. Claimed subjects keep two runs off the same topic.
lib/articles/agentSteps.ts:79 Each fresh session gets the topic, the registry material, the standard resolved now and the operator's rework note restated in its own brief and inputs.
lib/articles/agentSteps.ts:142 Every turn gets a fresh mkdtemp workspace. A predecessor's output is handed over under a name that says what it is (previous-post), not left in place.
lib/articles/resume.ts:22 A resumed run keeps its identity and its completed steps, and goes back to the state whose step did not finish.

lib/articles/types.ts:143 The critique panel spans providers, reviewers are blind to each other (engine.ts header) and rounds are capped at two. The panel driver itself (critiqueStep.ts) is outside this context.
lib/articles/loop.ts:388 The recovery budget is fixed at dispatch, and a run that hits its ceiling goes to a human and is never auto-resumed.
lib/articles/loop.ts:32 Executors are local CLIs started through cliSeam in the same process tree. There is no remote executor plane.

pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: lib/producers/article.ts:125 One article drive is tracked by two state machines, the kernel job (jobMachine) and run.json (ARTICLE_STATUSES), and the binding copies kernel stops across by hand. The comment at line 360 admits the two can disagree (a job killed after its check leaves the run at the gate, unbooked), which is the two-truths defect session-registry forbids.

techniques.evidence: lib/producers/article.ts:360 Two registries for one session. Readers must join the job and run.json, and the binding settles the disagreement case by case.
lib/producers/article.ts:354 Second drivers are refused under the kernel's fenced seat.text slot lease. One writer per run.
lib/producers/article.ts:371 A resume is a retry of the same job id, so the session's identity survives the fresh process.
lib/producers/article.ts:340 An interrupted job is treated as an unresolved outcome that may have spent, and it is retried only by an operator.
lib/producers/article.ts:393 A job that was not driven is a named outcome, not a silent success.

pairs.subject: fleet-orchestration
pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/src/slots/sweep-core.ts:69 When a publishing claim's heartbeat budget expires (stale) or its lease is absent, the sweep takes the fence from the claimant and fails the slot with "interrupted before the publish finished". The expired budget therefore lands on a terminal verdict that asserts non-completion, and a slow-but-alive uploader loses its guarded section, which is the failure evidence-outranks-a-liveness-claim names (land on unknown and label the outcome unresolved).

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/slots/sweep-core.ts:69 A stale claim is treated like an absent one and goes to failed (sweep.ts:27, core.ts:55 "dead claimant"). No evidence the upload itself wrote is consulted, and there is no unknown outcome.
packages/kernel/src/slots/sweep.ts:34 Two tiers: the publisher heartbeats per chunk, and the sweep fills the gap on a TTL.
packages/kernel/src/slots/sweep.ts:20 The claim, its owner and its fence commit with the state change, so ownership is part of the record.
packages/kernel/src/records/launch.ts:25 A run record and its job are committed in one transaction before anything can act on them.

pairs.registryProposal: evidence-outranks-a-liveness-claim could say how it meets at-most-once external effects (a publish upload): here the code deliberately fails a stale claim instead of leaving it unknown, so that nothing re-fires it. The technique should say whether an unknown-and-held state (no auto re-fire, operator resolves) is the required alternative, so that both properties hold.
